description: Source governance rules for News Dispatch. These rules define minimum evidence expectations, publication modes, and required caution by stream, source class and claim type. They do not replace editorial judgment.

official_source.description: Regulators, laws, courts, official records, public company releases, official blogs, filings and primary documents.

business_media.description: Reliable business media used for context, corroboration and source-reported claims.

public_media.description: General public media used as public signal and context, not as proof of high-impact claims by itself.

specialized_media.description: Industry media and trade publications. Useful for early signal detection; primary-source checks are required for strong conclusions.

research_media.description: Scientific journals, research media, papers, preprints, lab reports and research explainers.

community_source.description: Telegram, X, Reddit, forums, comments, reviews and community posts. These are never fact base by themselves.

marketing_source.description: Vendor marketing, sponsored material, landing pages and promotional claims. Treat as claims, not proof.

publication_modes.published: Reader-facing issue. Requires completed editorial review and source sufficiency for its stream.
publication_modes.limited_publication: Reader-facing but explicitly limited. Used when the signal is useful but evidence gaps remain.
publication_modes.draft_only: Non-reader-facing draft. Used for synthesis, source review and taxonomy testing.
publication_modes.blocked: Must not be published until source, safety or editorial blockers are resolved.

claim_rules.confirmed_fact: Needs primary source or official record unless the fact is only about a source item appearing in a public feed.
claim_rules.source_reported_claim: May be based on a named public source, but must not be written as independently verified fact.
claim_rules.corroborated_signal: Needs at least two meaningfully independent sources or one primary source plus one secondary source.
claim_rules.research_result: Must identify peer-reviewed, preprint, corporate lab report, benchmark report, survey or unknown status.
claim_rules.benchmark_result: Needs methodology, tested configuration and limits. Vendor-only benchmarks are marketing claims until independently checked.
claim_rules.community_signal: Needs pattern classification. Isolated complaints do not justify broad conclusions.
claim_rules.weak_signal: Must include confidence, what would confirm it and what would falsify it.
claim_rules.rumor: Not publishable as fact. Can appear only in a clearly marked weak-signal section if public-safe.
claim_rules.forecast: Must be framed as scenario or forecast, not as fact or investment guidance.
claim_rules.marketing_claim: Vendor claim to verify. Never proof by itself.
claim_rules.editorial_inference: Must be tied to evidence and include uncertainty or verification gap.
